women_risk_factors: History of pre-eclampsia: a recognised heart risk factor in women.
Hypertension in pregnancy: a recognised heart risk factor in women.
Gestational diabetes: raises later cardiovascular risk.
general_risk_factors: Diabetes: heart attacks may present without typical chest pain.

refs.troponin: ESC 2023 ACS guidelines: hs-troponin 0h/1h or 0h/2h algorithm; single-test rule-out only if very low and chest pain began >3 h earlier
refs.troponin_sex: High-STEACS (Shah et al., BMJ 2015): a female-specific hs-troponin threshold identified twice as many women with myocardial infarction
refs.ecg: Fourth Universal Definition of MI (2018): ST elevation thresholds, women ≥1.5 mm in V2–V3
refs.no_ecg: NICE CG95: anyone with suspected acute coronary syndrome should have a 12-lead ECG as soon as possible
refs.ecg_subtle: Women's ST elevation is often smaller (VIRGO study, JAHA 2018); STEMI criteria miss many occlusions in both sexes
refs.pregnancy_risk: ESC 2024 hypertension guidelines: pregnancy complications are sex-specific cardiovascular risk modifiers
refs.scad: ESC position paper on SCAD (2018): SCAD causes many heart attacks in young women and around pregnancy
refs.menopause: ESC 2021 prevention guidelines: premature menopause raises cardiovascular risk
refs.diabetes: ESC 2023 ACS guidelines: patients with diabetes often present without typical chest pain
refs.repeat: Repeat attendance with unexplained symptoms is a recognised red flag for missed diagnosis

rules.safety_net_message: You have been seen in A&E today. Please call 999 straight away if you get pain or pressure in your chest, jaw, neck, arm or back, breathlessness, sweating, or nausea that does not go away. In women these can be signs of a heart attack even without severe chest pain. If you are worried, do not wait: it is always right to come back.
history_questions: Ever had pre-eclampsia or high blood pressure in pregnancy?
Pregnant now, or given birth in the last 12 months?
Been to A&E with similar symptoms before?

Sarah, 44.story: Came to A&E with fatigue, breathlessness and chest pain. ECG and troponin done straight away: On admission her ECG shows no ST elevation and her troponin is below the threshold. She is anxious and breathing fast, so a panic attack seems likely.
Sarah, 44.triage_note: Chest pain, breathless, exhausted for 2 days. Very anxious, breathing fast.
timeline_without: No ST elevation on ECG; troponin below threshold; symptoms fit a panic attack
Pain and breathlessness return; she waits, told it was anxiety
Collapses at home; 999; heart attack with permanent heart muscle damage
timeline_with: Discharge pressed; Second Look: troponin too early to rule out, pre-eclampsia, repeat visit
Repeat troponin ordered; she stays in A&E
Cardiology review and treatment, about 2 days earlier
